functions.name: Security overview
functions.detail: The starting point for any ticker: live quote, day and 52-week range, price chart, fundamentals, and tabs into every other research pane. A bond fund shows its SEC yield, yield to worst and duration beside its distribution yield, and --tax-rate 40.8 adds a muni fund's tax-equivalent yield and muni/Treasury ratio. T is the same pane; search Ticker Research to open a second one.

functions.name: Quote monitor
functions.detail: A compact board of live quotes for any list of tickers, each with change, range, and a sparkline. Good as the always-open strip in a layout.

functions.name: Price chart
functions.detail: A price chart with volume in the chart composer, defaulting to a multi-year range. Add indicators, drawings, or other series from the same pane.

functions.name: Intraday chart
functions.detail: One or five sessions of intraday candles with the session boundaries marked. Real-time on Pro, 15-minute delayed on Free.

functions.name: Time and sales
functions.detail: Recent prints from the consolidated tape with time, price, size, venue, and conditions; prints of 10,000 shares or more stand out. US equities, real-time on Pro, 15-minute delayed on Free.

functions.name: Quote recap
functions.detail: NBBO history: bid and ask with sizes, venues, and spread in basis points, plus the median and widest spread and locked or crossed quotes. The NBBO tab of TAS.

functions.name: Custom chart
functions.detail: The chart composer with an explicit series list: prices, statement lines, valuation multiples, FRED series, indicators, and formulas on shared or separate axes. Series read SYMBOL:field or FRED:series, as in NVDA:price, FRED:CPIAUCSL; start empty to search the catalog.

functions.name: Data catalog
functions.detail: Searches every series the chart composer knows: securities, options, crypto, FRED, treasuries, and futures. Pick one to chart it.

functions.name: Financial analysis
functions.detail: Annual and quarterly statements with the line items you expect, plus derived margins and growth. Switch periods and statements with the tabs.

functions.name: Credit documents
functions.detail: Instrument balances, maturities, covenants, change-of-control terms and amendment history with primary-document evidence. Pro includes the full dataset; free access previews three instruments.

functions.name: Covenants
functions.detail: Maintenance tests and disclosed financial metrics, with headroom only when contractual definitions and borrower scope match. Screen for low headroom and upcoming springing maturities.

functions.name: Debt maturities
functions.detail: Principal due in the next 12 months, in each of years two to five, and after, from the latest annual filing, with the near-term share ranked against 10 years. A newer 10-Q adds its current and non-current debt. History tracks principal and interest expense.

functions.name: Historical prices
functions.detail: Daily open, high, low, close, and volume in a scrollable table, exportable to CSV from pane settings.

functions.name: Compare performance
functions.detail: Price returns rebased to a shared start date for two or more tickers, so relative performance is readable at a glance. A leveraged or inverse fund also gets the k× daily line of its index fund (3× daily QQQ beside TQQQ) and its decay against it, in percentage points.

functions.name: Fundamental graph
functions.detail: Quarterly revenue for one or more companies as grouped columns, with any other statement field one click away in the series editor.

functions.name: Valuation graph
functions.detail: Trailing P/E history for one or more tickers; switch to forward P/E, PEG, P/S, EV/EBITDA, or P/FCF in the series editor.

functions.name: Relationship graph
functions.detail: How two tickers move together: indexed prices, their ratio, rolling correlation, and a return regression with beta, alpha, and R².

functions.name: Correlation matrix
functions.detail: A date-aligned Pearson correlation matrix of daily returns for a basket, useful for checking how diversified a set of names really is.

functions.name: Backtest
functions.detail: Tests a long-only rule on daily history against buy-and-hold: a preset like golden cross or RSI, or your own, like rsi(14) < 30. Equity and drawdown curves, CAGR, Sharpe, and every trade. BTST opens it too.

functions.name: Relative valuation
functions.detail: Compare market cap, P/E, EV/sales, growth, and margins. The pane auto-picks peers when opened on one ticker. The CLI compares the tickers given unless you add --peers; add --columns evEbitda for optional EV/EBITDA.

functions.name: Equity screener
functions.detail: Filter covered stocks on valuation, growth, margins, liquidity, short interest, insider activity, and 13F holders, then rank the matches by any metric. Exports to CSV; saving a screen needs a verified email.

functions.name: Options monitor
functions.detail: Calls and puts by expiry with bid, ask, volume, open interest, implied volatility, and Greeks. Real-time on Pro.

functions.name: Options positioning
functions.detail: Open interest by strike with max pain, each expiry's put/call ratio and net dealer gamma, and dealer gamma by strike with its flip level and call and put walls. Open interest is about two sessions old; the footer names its date. GEX and MAXPAIN open it too.

functions.name: Options calculator
functions.detail: Price a European call or put from spot, strike, rate, volatility, and expiry, or solve for implied volatility from a market price.

functions.name: Options scenario
functions.detail: Build a multi-leg options position from the chain, from OMON, or by hand, and value it at any spot, date, and vol shift: payoff, P&L grid, breakevens, and Greeks. It also sells a cash-secured put, with the yield on cash at the mid and at the bid, sizes a protective put to a hedge budget, and collars shares. European pricing, so no early exercise.

functions.name: Options strategy screen
functions.description: Puts, covered calls, spreads, condors, straddles and calendars across a list
functions.detail: One tab per strategy: cash-secured put, covered call, vertical, iron condor, straddle, strangle and calendar. For each ticker it picks the legs by delta and expiry, then shows credit or debit, max gain and loss, break-evens, probability of profit, IV rank, wide spreads and earnings before expiry. Income trades rank by yearly return, debit trades by reward to risk.

functions.name: Volatility surface
functions.detail: The implied volatility surface fitted from option quotes: 3D sheet, table, smiles, ATM term structure, 25-delta skew, and forwards. Steps back through stored daily closes; live is real-time on Pro, 15-minute delayed on Free.

functions.name: Implied volatility history
functions.detail: Daily 30- and 90-day at-the-money implied vol since February 2024 against realized vol, with the spread and each measure's 52-week rank and percentile. A new ticker backfills in a few minutes.

functions.name: Realized volatility
functions.detail: Rolling realized volatility over windows from 10 to 260 sessions, with price and today's at-the-money IV for reference. Five estimators, from close-to-close to Yang-Zhang.

functions.name: Volatility cone
functions.detail: Each window's realized volatility against its one- or two-year range, as a cone and a table, with today's at-the-money IV on top: is vol high for this name? The Cone tab of HVG.

functions.name: Seasonality
functions.detail: Monthly returns for each year as a heatmap, every month's average, median and share of up years, each year's path laid over one January-to-December axis, and a Weekdays tab with the average return, up share and session count for each weekday and the turn of the month.

functions.name: Volatility rich/cheap
functions.detail: IV rank, term slope, skew, and IV against realized vol for up to 60 US tickers, flagged rich or cheap against each name's own year. Without tickers it screens index and sector ETFs.

functions.name: Analyst research
functions.detail: Consensus price target with the range, the rating distribution, and recent upgrades, downgrades, and initiations by firm.

functions.name: Earnings estimates
functions.detail: Quarterly and annual EPS and revenue estimates next to reported results, with beats and misses.

functions.name: Estimate revisions
functions.detail: Consensus EPS by quarter and year with its latest change, 30-day up and down revisions, and range; open a period to chart it. Surprises and Guidance tabs too. EEO opens it too.

functions.name: Company KPIs
functions.detail: Company-reported operating metrics by fiscal period, with native currencies, definitions, charts, source quotes and retained restatements. Three latest series are free to preview; full history is Pro.

functions.name: Guidance tracker
functions.detail: Management guidance as dated ranges and points, with raises, cuts, withdrawals and later actuals when the period and accounting basis match. Cited evidence and revision history. Three current guides are free to preview; full coverage is Pro.

functions.name: Company guidance
functions.detail: The outlook the company gave on its latest earnings call, above consensus for the coming periods. US listings. The Guidance tab of EM.

functions.name: Corporate actions
functions.detail: Dividend and split history plus past and upcoming earnings dates and estimates in one timeline.

functions.name: Dividend yield
functions.detail: Cash distributions, trailing yield, indicated rate when available, and payout growth. A bond fund's distribution yield is labelled as not its SEC yield, which follows it dated with yield to worst and duration; --tax-rate 40.8 adds a muni fund's tax-equivalent yield and muni/Treasury ratio. Several tickers rank in one table, with those columns too under --tax-rate. Future payments are not forecast.

functions.name: Short interest
functions.detail: Bi-monthly FINRA settlement data with shares short, days to cover, and average daily volume over time.

functions.name: Daily short volume
functions.detail: FINRA daily off-exchange short volume as a share of volume, charted against its one-year range. Not short interest; SI has that.

functions.name: Fails to deliver
functions.detail: The Short Interest pane on Fails to deliver: SEC outstanding fail shares by settlement date and CUSIP, with reported prices. Each date is a separate snapshot; never add fails across dates. Published twice monthly with a delay. Missing records do not establish zero fails.

functions.name: Weekly ATS / OTC volume
functions.detail: The Short Interest pane on Weekly ATS/OTC: FINRA ATS and non-ATS shares and trades, including dark-pool activity. ATS % divides ATS shares by published off-exchange shares, not total market volume or short volume. Missing categories stay blank. Published weekly with a two- or four-week delay depending on the security tier.

functions.name: Equity diagnostic
functions.detail: A read of the company's filings and numbers into red flags, anomalies, green flags, and items to watch, each with the evidence it came from.

functions.name: Risk factors
functions.detail: The 10-K risk factor section grouped by theme, with the items that were added, dropped, or rewritten since the prior year called out.

functions.name: Executives
functions.description: Officers and pay from the proxy
functions.detail: Named executive officers and their compensation. Free shows each executive's total pay; Pro adds the breakdown and earlier years.

functions.name: 8-K filings
functions.detail: The company's 8-Ks classified by item (agreements, executive changes, auditor changes, restructurings) with a summary of what each one said.

functions.name: Earnings calls
functions.detail: Earnings call transcripts with speaker attribution, the analyst Q&A, and guidance and notable quotes. Without a ticker it lists new calls as they land.

functions.name: Hiring momentum
functions.detail: Weekly open roles, role and location mix, remote share, hiring changes and peers for one company. Pro shows the full history; Free shows the latest values and three rows per section.

functions.name: App attention
functions.description: App ranks, ratings and company momentum
functions.detail: Public app chart ranks by storefront, matched rank velocity, rating drift, country spreads and listed-parent comparisons. Open an app for its rank history.

functions.name: Hiring
functions.description: Open roles, by function, over time
functions.detail: Open roles read daily from a company's own careers site: trend, function, country, seniority, new roles, pay ranges and themes such as AI. Without a ticker it ranks every covered company.

functions.name: Research search
functions.detail: Full-text search across earnings call transcripts, news wires, and SEC filings, with the matching passage inline. Free with an account; alerts on a saved search's new hits are Pro.

functions.name: AI screener
functions.detail: Describe a screen in plain language and get a table of matching tickers, saved as a reusable tab. Uses the AI provider you configure.

functions.name: AI agent
functions.detail: A long-running AI thread with your choice of model that can read your panes and run research commands for you.

functions.name: Ask Gloom
functions.detail: Ask a question about what is on screen and watch the tools Gloom runs to answer it. Requires a verified Cloud account.

functions.name: Top news
functions.detail: Curated stories ranked by importance across wires, publishers, and X, with tickers and category. The pane to keep open when you only want what matters.

functions.name: News feed
functions.detail: Every story as it arrives, newest first, with source, tickers, sentiment, and importance score; filter by sentiment or minimum score. Add News Feed adds your own RSS feed (desktop and terminal, not web).

functions.name: Ticker news
functions.detail: Stories linked to the selected ticker, newest first.

functions.name: Topic news
functions.description: News by topic code or sector
functions.detail: Market news by topic code (MNA, CB, ENERGY, METALS, REG, CRYPTO, EARN, IPO) or by sector. LTR lists public fund and investor letters as links to the publisher's page.

functions.name: Breaking news
functions.detail: Stories flagged as breaking or urgent. Turn on Notifications in its pane settings to hear about new ones even while the pane is closed.

functions.name: X feed
functions.detail: An X advanced-search feed for any ticker or query with likes and views, refreshed live. Needs a verified email.

functions.name: Social mentions
functions.description: Daily X posts naming a cashtag
functions.detail: Daily posts on X naming the ticker's cashtag, the day's top posts and their stance.

functions.name: Substack
functions.detail: Your Substack subscriptions as a reader feed inside the terminal, signed in with your own account.

functions.name: Live TV
functions.detail: Live financial television in a pane (desktop and terminal with a capable renderer).

functions.name: Hacker News
functions.detail: Top, New, Best, Show, and Ask with scores and comment counts. Also the reference plugin if you want to write your own.

functions.name: Market movers
functions.detail: Today's top gainers, losers, most active and trending tickers with price, change, volume against average and market cap, and the pre-market and after-hours movers. Pro adds the gaps at the open.

functions.name: World equity indices
functions.detail: Major indices grouped by region with last, change, and session status, so you can see which markets are open and how they closed.

functions.name: Sector performance
functions.detail: S&P 500 sectors and industries sorted by the day's move, with their representative ETFs.

functions.name: Index and ETF members
functions.description: ETF holdings, member returns and index changes
functions.detail: Holdings of SPY, QQQ, IVV, IWM and other index, sector, thematic and bond ETFs, with weights, member returns, daily contributions and index changes. Leveraged funds, USO and BITO list their swaps and futures, bond funds their bonds, and the gold, silver and crypto trusts the metal or coin they hold. SPX uses IVV holdings.

functions.name: Relative rotation
functions.detail: Each name's strength against SPY or another benchmark, plotted against its momentum with weekly trails through the four quadrants. Sector ETFs by default, or your tickers. GRR opens it too.

functions.name: Market heatmap
functions.detail: The 500 largest US stocks grouped by sector and industry, or the largest ETFs, as a treemap colored by the day's move and moving with live quotes. Sized by the square root of market cap, or by market cap itself.

functions.name: FX cross rates
functions.detail: A cross-rate matrix for the major currencies, updated live.

functions.name: Crypto board
functions.detail: The top 100 coins by market cap, with returns from a day to a year, a 30-day sparkline, volume, and market cap. Stablecoins have their own tab: total supply over time stacked by coin, and each coin's supply, 7- and 30-day supply growth and share of the total. Prices stream live on every plan where the market allows.

functions.name: Layer 2 metrics
functions.detail: Ethereum and its layer 2 chains side by side: transactions, active addresses, fees, transaction cost, stablecoin supply and value secured, with 30-day changes and a daily history chart. Data from growthepie.

functions.name: Crypto ETF flows
functions.description: Daily spot bitcoin and ether ETF flows
functions.detail: Daily net flows of the US spot bitcoin and ether ETFs, fund by fund in US$ millions, as Farside Investors publishes them: the last 5 and 20 days, the running total since launch, and the funds the newest day still waits on.

functions.name: Perpetuals
functions.description: Perpetual funding, open interest and premium
functions.detail: A board and rankings of perpetuals on Hyperliquid, Binance, Bybit and OKX, one asset across the venues, and one perpetual's funding, open interest and premium history with each reading's source. Pro shows the history; Free a limited preview. Trading is in the Hyperliquid plugin.

functions.name: Futures board
functions.detail: Each root's front contract until its stated roll date across equity index, volatility (VIX futures, at Cboe's daily settlement), rates, energy, metals, agriculture, and FX with last price, unit and session change, grouped by sector, naming the day's most active month by volume when it is another one.

functions.name: Futures curve
functions.detail: A futures root's listed contracts as a curve against a week and a month ago, with roll yield, contango or backwardation, and each contract's price, open interest, and volume. CTM VIX is the VIX futures curve from Cboe's daily settlements, with spot VIX and the front month's premium to it. Ann. roll yield is what a long position earns or pays rolling from the front contract into the next, scaled to a year: (front / next - 1) × 365 / days between the two, positive in backwardation and negative in contango. PCTL ranks a figure against its own daily values over the past year, 100 the highest and 0 the lowest: the roll yield and the front spread against theirs, and in the table each contract's price against its own.

functions.name: Fear and greed
functions.detail: The CNN Fear & Greed index with its history and each of the seven component indicators.

functions.name: Crypto fear and greed
functions.detail: The crypto Fear and Greed Index from Alternative.me: today's reading, yesterday, last week and last month, and its history.

functions.name: Commitments of Traders positioning
functions.detail: Weekly CFTC and ICE Futures Europe Commitments of Traders (Brent, gasoil and more): net positioning by trader class, the weekly change, and one- and three-year percentiles. Pass a root like CL to chart it under the front-month price. CFTC opens it too.

functions.name: Power and grid buildout
functions.detail: Grid interconnection queues, datacentre and other large-load requests, generation capacity and utility exposure, with a link to the source for every project. Pro shows the full data and history; Free shows three rows per section. EPWR opens the Prices tab, free: day-ahead power prices for 32 European markets in EUR/MWh and the EU carbon (EUA) auction clearing price in EUR/tCO2, each with its daily history. EPWR GAS shows European gas storage from GIE AGSI+: % full, TWh and daily injection and withdrawal for the EU and each member state, against a year ago and the five-year range.

functions.name: Exposure engine
functions.detail: Apply country, supplier, customer, tariff, commodity, rate and FX shocks to holdings and see exposure ranges and the paths behind them. Free previews one holding and one hop; Pro covers 100 holdings and four hops.

functions.name: GPU Rental Prices
functions.detail: What it costs to rent a GPU by the hour: published prices, spot rates and marketplace asks in USD per GPU-hour, with history and related equities. Pro shows the full board; Free shows a three-row sample led by H100, B200 and H200.

functions.name: Government awards
functions.detail: Government awards, subcontractors and modifications with verified company matches, native-currency amounts, agency concentration, sector rankings, cumulative obligations and primary-source evidence. Pro includes filters and history; everyone can view a three-row preview.

functions.name: Revenue breakdown
functions.detail: Quarterly revenue by product, segment or region from the company's 10-Q and 10-K filings. Free shows the first two lines; Pro shows every line.

functions.name: Reverse DCF
functions.detail: The yearly free cash flow growth over ten years that makes a DCF equal today's enterprise value, next to the growth the company actually delivered.

functions.name: P/E band
functions.detail: Weekly price against round multiples of trailing EPS, stepping when each EPS figure became known, with today's P/E ranked in the stock's own history.

functions.name: Returns
functions.detail: Interval and cumulative price returns in a scrollable table, for a range and granularity you pick.

functions.name: Macro-day reaction
functions.description: How a name moves on CPI, jobs, FOMC
functions.detail: A name's average move on CPI, jobs report and FOMC days against a normal day, with the share of up days and the move on every release day.

functions.name: Short squeeze watch
functions.description: Crowded shorts that are moving up
functions.detail: Short interest as a share of float, days to cover, the change since the prior settlement and the month's price move across your portfolios and watchlists, or the tickers you give. Updates twice a month.

functions.name: Earnings ripple
functions.description: Holdings tied to a company reporting soon
functions.detail: Customers your holdings name in their filings, and suppliers whose filings name your holdings, with the disclosed revenue share, by report date.

functions.name: Supply chain
functions.detail: Who a company buys from and sells to, with the filing, call or announcement behind each link: Table, Flow, Graph and Path views, up to four hops. Free previews three relationships per role; Pro shows everything.

functions.name: Catalysts
functions.detail: A calendar of regulatory, clinical, legal and trade-policy events linked to companies, with source documents and every revision. Free previews three events; Pro shows them all, with alerts.

functions.name: Litigation
functions.detail: One company's litigation, enforcement and antitrust cases, with primary documents and dated status changes. Free previews three events; Pro shows them all.

functions.name: Clinical trials
functions.description: Studies by condition, drug or sponsor
functions.detail: Clinical studies by condition, drug or sponsor, with status, phase and enrollment. Open a study for its full record.

functions.name: FDA reports
functions.detail: FDA drug and device adverse event reports and drug recalls, by drug, device or firm name. A report is what someone observed, not proof the product caused it.

functions.name: Oil and gas inventories
functions.detail: The EIA's weekly oil and natural gas storage: crude, Cushing, the SPR, products and gas by region, each with the week's build or draw and its place in the five-year range. NGS opens the gas tab.

functions.name: VIX term structure
functions.detail: Daily Cboe VIX closes from 9 days to a year out, with the three-month to 30-day ratio and its history, so you can see whether the term structure is in contango or inverted. The VIX futures curve, with spot VIX and the front month's premium to it, is CTM VIX.

functions.name: Cross-asset volatility
functions.detail: Volatility indices across assets on one board: the VIX term, VVIX, SKEW, MOVE, and index, commodity, and emerging-market vol, each with its one-year percentile. The Cross-asset tab of VIX.

functions.name: New highs and lows
functions.detail: A live count of stocks printing new session highs and lows over 30-second, one-minute, and five-minute windows. Real-time on Pro, 15-minute delayed on Free.

functions.name: Live scanner
functions.detail: Scan all US stocks, an index, a sector or a watchlist for your own conditions: a move over the last minutes, volume against its usual pace, a new session high or low, a VWAP cross or a gap, above price, market cap and volume floors. Matches refresh through the session and new ones can alert. Real-time on Pro, 15-minute delayed on Free.

functions.name: Options flow
functions.detail: Sweeps, blocks, and large premium prints, plus the session's net premium tide.

functions.name: Market halts
functions.detail: Current and recent US trading halts with the reason code and resumption times.

functions.name: IPO calendar
functions.detail: Upcoming and recently listed IPOs worldwide, with price in local currency, deal size in dollars, and first-day return.

functions.name: Thematic baskets
functions.detail: Curated themes with equal-weight returns and breadth. Open a theme for its members, leaders and laggards. The Themes tab of BI.

functions.name: M&A
functions.detail: Pending, rumored and closed mergers and acquisitions, with arbitrage spreads on listed targets. Free is delayed 7 days; Pro is live.

functions.name: Distress
functions.detail: Dated public records about companies in difficulty: 8-K bankruptcy, obligation and listing filings, SEC going-concern disclosures, Taiwan exchange listing designations, and French and UK insolvency notices. The Distress tab of MA.

functions.name: World venue map
functions.detail: Trading venues around the world with open or closed status, local time, and time to the next session change.

functions.name: Prediction markets
functions.detail: Browse and search Polymarket and Kalshi markets by category with top odds, spread, and volume, and chart any market's history.

functions.name: Adjacent indices
functions.detail: Adjacent's indices built on prediction markets, with each one's level and 1D and 7D moves, its chart and constituents, plus reference rates and CFTC filings.

functions.name: Polls
functions.detail: VoteHub polls by type (approval, favorability, generic ballot, Senate, governor, House) with trend charts and pollster breakdowns.

functions.name: Chokepoint transits
functions.detail: Daily vessel transits through the main shipping chokepoints, charted together or one by name. Use it to see a disruption in trade before it shows up in prices; each transit series also charts in G next to oil or a shipper.

functions.name: Economic calendar
functions.detail: Upcoming releases and central bank events with impact, country, actual, forecast, and prior.

functions.name: Economic statistics
functions.detail: Inflation, labour, growth, housing, and rates indicators with the latest print, the prior, and a chart against their own history.

functions.name: US consumer prices
functions.detail: US inflation by component (food, energy, core goods, shelter, services ex shelter) with each one's weight, monthly and yearly change, and points added to the headline. The header gives the next release. ECAN opens it too.

functions.name: Central bank rates
functions.detail: Policy rates for the G20 central banks, the SNB, Norges Bank, the Riksbank and the RBNZ with the last move, its date, and a one-year percentile; open one for its history. ECFC and CBRT open it too.

functions.name: Yield curves
functions.detail: Government yield curves: US Treasury, TIPS real yields and breakevens, euro AAA, Bund, Gilt, JGB and Canada, with spreads like 2s10s and their one-year percentiles, a two-date difference and a World tab that adds Mexico's and Brazil's 2- and 10-year yields. GC JGB opens a curve directly.

functions.name: US rate path
functions.detail: The fed funds rate priced for each upcoming FOMC meeting from futures, against a week and a month ago and the Fed's projections, with per-meeting probabilities. FFIP opens it too.

functions.name: Credit spreads
functions.detail: ICE BofA US corporate option-adjusted spreads by rating bucket and high yield, with the day's change.

functions.name: Treasury auctions
functions.detail: US Treasury bill, note, bond, and TIPS auction results since 1979: rate, stop-out versus median, bid-to-cover, bidder takedown, and size. An after view ranks each auction against its tenor's last 24 and shows the Treasury yield's move 1, 5, and 20 sessions later. Hong Kong's Exchange Fund Bills and Notes and Government Bond tenders too.

functions.name: Money markets
functions.detail: Funding rates (SOFR, EFFR, IORB), Treasury bill yields and their curve, and Fed liquidity from reserves to the reverse repo, each with its one-year percentile and history.

functions.name: Single-name CDS
functions.detail: Single-name corporate CDS. CDS alone lists the issuers traded in the last 5 days with trade count, last trade, 5Y spread and its 1W and 1M moves through the roll while the level is current (points upfront past 2,000 bp), ranked with --sort spread, 1w or 1m; with a ticker or issuer, its 5Y spread (level, date, 1W and 1M change, range), its trades and its daily 5Y levels (--csv --section daily exports them).

functions.name: Index CDS
functions.detail: CDX IG, HY and EM with iTraxx Main and Crossover on the run, and CMBX A, BBB- and BB on the newest series: the level, 1D and 1W moves, 1Y percentile and the day's print count. IG and iTraxx in spread, HY, EM and CMBX in price.

functions.name: Sovereign CDS
functions.detail: Sovereign 5Y CDS ranked by the month's move, beside the local currency's move against the dollar, with each country's year of history. WCDS opens it too.

functions.name: Bond calculator
functions.detail: Price a fixed-coupon bond from a yield, or solve the yield from a price: accrued interest, duration, convexity, DV01, spread to Treasuries, cash flows, and price at yield shifts.

functions.name: Fixed Income
functions.detail: One workspace for credit markets, issuer debt, corporate bond sales, Treasury auctions, Treasury cash and debt, and primary dealer positions. FI opens it; the older shortcuts still land on their own section.

functions.name: Corporate bond tape
functions.description: Corporate and agency sales by issuer or CUSIP
functions.detail: Latest corporate and agency bond sales: issuer, CUSIP, coupon, maturity, price, yield, and grade. TRACE alone lists the tape; TRACE with an issuer name, a bond symbol root, a stock ticker, or a CUSIP finds that issuer's outstanding bonds. It opens the Bonds section of Fixed Income.

functions.name: Treasury cash and debt
functions.description: Operating cash and debt held by the public
functions.detail: Treasury operating cash for the latest day, and debt held by the public for the last 20 business days. It opens the Treasury section of Fixed Income.

functions.name: Primary dealer positions
functions.detail: Weekly net positions and settlement fails in Treasuries and mortgage-backed securities, from the primary dealers. It opens the Treasury section of Fixed Income.

functions.name: Market valuation
functions.detail: Market-wide valuation ratios against their own history, with zones and trend deviation.

functions.name: Earnings calendar
functions.detail: Upcoming earnings dates and estimates grouped by when they report, with implied and past moves. Alone it follows your portfolio and watchlists; with tickers, just those. EVTS opens it too.

functions.name: SEC filings
functions.detail: Recent SEC filings for a ticker with form type and date; open any of them inline. US equities only.

functions.name: Holders
functions.detail: Institutional holders as a table (value, shares, change, percent held) or as an ownership treemap.

functions.name: 13F funds
functions.detail: Browse institutional 13F filings by fund, ticker, or CIK with estimated long-book performance, holdings, and filing history. Option values are underlying notional, not market value.

functions.name: Insider transactions
functions.description: Form 4 activity, insider buying and selling
functions.detail: Insider buys, sells, awards, and gifts from Form 4 filings with insider name, size, and price. pages.title: Install Gloom: Mac, Windows, Linux, TUI
pages.lead: Install the Gloom desktop app on Mac or Windows, or run it in a terminal with one command. Then update it and confirm it runs.

blocks.text: Either command installs the desktop app and the `gloom` terminal command.

blocks.code:
brew install --cask gloom
# or
curl -fsSL gloom.sh/install | bash

blocks.text: Or use the [direct download](/download/desktop). The desktop app and the Homebrew cask (`brew install --cask gloom`) need Apple Silicon. On an Intel Mac, the script installs the terminal UI only.
The [script](https://github.com/gloom-sh/gloomberb/blob/main/scripts/install.sh) checks the release's SHA-256 and edits no shell file.
Coming from Bloomberg? [What runs on a Mac](/answers/bloomberg-terminal-on-mac).
The terminal UI. Ghostty, Kitty or WezTerm draw charts best.

blocks.code: curl -fsSL gloom.sh/install | bash

blocks.text: Run the [desktop installer](/download/desktop). If SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. With Smart App Control on, use [term.gloom.sh](https://term.gloom.sh) instead.

blocks.code: irm https://gloom.sh/install.ps1 | iex

blocks.text: Then open a new terminal window.

items: **Checksum:** compare `Get-FileHash` on the installer with the SHA-256 on the [release page](https://github.com/gloom-sh/gloomberb/releases/latest).
**Plugins from GitHub**, such as Interactive Brokers, need [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win).
**Versions:** Windows 11 x64 is tested. Windows on Arm runs the x64 build.

blocks.text: [Open term.gloom.sh](https://term.gloom.sh). No account needed: search, charts and most panes, with quotes 15 minutes delayed and news 12 hours delayed.
A free sign-in adds filings, scanners and sync. Brokers and local plugins need the app.
Open the desktop app, or run `gloom` for the terminal UI. If it does not start, run `gloom doctor`: it checks settings, the cache and plugins.
The apps update themselves. **Check for Updates** in the command bar checks now. Homebrew: `brew upgrade --cask gloom`. Bun: `bun install -g @gloom-sh/terminal@latest`.
An install from before 0.18.4 has the `gloomberb` command. Updating adds `gloom` beside it, and `Gloomberb.app` becomes `Gloom.app`. Settings and data stay.
Updates come from **stable** releases, the ones on the [changelog](/changelog). **Nightly** is a daily build that can break. **Release Channel** in the command bar switches.
Quit Gloom, then remove it the way you installed it:

items: **Homebrew:** `brew uninstall --cask gloom`. Add `--zap` to delete your data too.
**macOS install script:** `rm -rf /Applications/Gloom.app ~/.local/bin/gloom ~/.local/bin/gloomberb`. A direct download: drag `Gloom.app` to the Trash.
**Linux:** `rm -f ~/.local/bin/gloom ~/.local/bin/gloomberb`
**Windows:** **Settings > Apps**, Gloom, **Uninstall**. For the PowerShell line, delete `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\gloom.exe`.
**Bun:** `bun remove -g @gloom-sh/terminal`

blocks.text: Your data stays unless you delete it.

blocks.summary: Where Gloom keeps its data, and the small print

blocks.text: Gloom keeps its data in `~/.gloomberb` (`%USERPROFILE%\.gloomberb` on Windows), or the XDG folders on a new Linux install. The Mac app also keeps these, which `--zap` deletes:

blocks.code:
~/Library/Application Support/com.vincelwt.gloomberb
~/Library/Preferences/com.vincelwt.gloomberb.plist
~/Library/WebKit/com.vincelwt.gloomberb

blocks.text: Your Gloom account stays until you delete it in the app.

pages.title: Your first Gloom session
pages.lead: Build a market workspace in ten minutes, and learn the four ideas the rest of Gloom uses.

blocks.text: Search Apple, open a chart, add market movers, name the layout. The desktop app and the terminal use the same commands.
Press backtick, type `Apple` and pick the NASDAQ listing.

blocks.alt: Ticker search showing Apple listings inside Gloom
blocks.caption: Each match shows its type and exchange.

blocks.text: Press `Cmd/Ctrl+K`, type `GP AAPL` and press Enter. Forgot a code? Type `Graph Price`.

blocks.alt: Gloom command bar showing the GP AAPL Graph Price command
blocks.caption: The command bar takes codes and plain names.

blocks.text: Open the command bar again and run `MOST`.

blocks.caption: MOST: gainers, losers, active and trending.

blocks.text: Drag a pane's title to move it and an edge to resize it, or run `GL` to tile them all.
The layout saves as you go. Run **Rename Layout** and type `Morning Research`. `Cmd/Ctrl+1` to `9` switch layouts.

blocks.caption: Company research, a price chart and market movers.

blocks.text: Run `gloom` and follow the same steps, with `Ctrl+P` for the command bar. Chart not drawing? See [troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting#chart-or-terminal-graphics).

items: The **command bar** runs functions and finds tickers. [All functions](/docs/functions) lists them.
A **pane** shows one thing. A **layout** groups panes for one job, and `LAY` lists layouts.
`F1` explains the focused pane, and `DOCS GP` opens these docs in the app.

blocks.text: Each pane's footer says how fresh its data is: **15m delayed** on Free, **real-time** on Pro where the pane supports it. **Stale** means a refresh failed: press `r`.
Gloom runs without an account. [Gloom Cloud](/docs/cloud-and-data) adds sync, chat and Pro.

pages.title: Goal-based workflows
pages.lead: Short recipes for a market check, company research, peer comparison, earnings, macro, the AI buildout and dry-bulk freight.

blocks.text: Run each code in the command bar. `GL` tiles what you opened.

items: `MOST`: what is moving
`TOP`: the stories that matter
`ECO`: the macro releases coming up
`ERN`: who in your portfolio reports soon

blocks.caption: MOST: gainers, losers, active and trending.

items: `DES AAPL`: profile, quote and performance
`GP AAPL`: the price chart
`FA AAPL`: statements and ratios
`SEC AAPL` and `CN AAPL`: filings and company news
`NOTE`: a scratchpad for what you found
`CMP AAPL, MSFT, GOOG`: price performance
`RV AAPL, MSFT, GOOG`: valuation and operating metrics
`CORR AAPL, MSFT, GOOG`: how their returns move together

blocks.caption: RV compares valuation across a peer group.

items: `ERN AAPL, MSFT, NVDA`: dates and estimates
`EE AAPL`: EPS and revenue estimates
`ANR AAPL`: analyst targets and actions
`CPI`: what is driving inflation
`WIRP`: the rate path futures price in
`GC`: government yield curves
`DOE`: weekly oil and gas inventories
`GPU H100`: what a GPU costs to rent
`POWER`: power waiting to connect to the grid
`SPLC NVDA` and `JOBS NVDA`: who it buys from and sells to, and what it hires for
`EXPO`: what a shock does to your holdings

blocks.text: These are Pro, with a preview on Free except `JOBS`.

items: `GP BDRY`: a freight futures fund, the closest traded read of rates
`CMP SBLK, GNK, DSX`: shipowners side by side
`CHOKE`: daily transits through Suez, Panama, Hormuz and other straits

pages.title: Portfolios and rebalancing
pages.lead: Track what you hold in PF, give each holding a target weight, and see the trade that brings it back.

blocks.alt: PF with target weights: each holding's weight, target, drift and trade
blocks.caption: VTI is 8.2pp over its 50% target, so PF says sell 6 shares.

items: Run **New Portfolio** from the command bar.
Choose **Manual**, or a broker to sync its positions.
Name it, then open it with `PF`.
In `PF`, press `a`, type or paste tickers, and press Enter.
Run **Set Portfolio Position** to give a holding its shares and average cost. `AP` does the same for the ticker you are on.
Bought in another currency? Fill in **Purchase Date** or **Cost FX** so P&L includes the currency's move.
Download your positions page as a CSV. Fidelity, Schwab, Vanguard, E*TRADE and Merrill exports work, as does any table with symbol and quantity columns.
In `PF`, open the pane menu (`.` or the `...` button) and choose **Import Positions…**.
Check the preview, choose a new portfolio, **Merge** or **Replace**, then **Import**.

blocks.text: Put the cursor on a holding, press `t` and type its weight: `60` for 60%. Cash takes one on its `CASH` row. `Shift+T` clears a target.
Once a holding has a target, `PF` adds these columns after the ticker:

rows: Share of the total, cash included
Weight minus target, in percentage points
Shares to buy (+) or sell (-) to reach the target

blocks.text: Trades use the current price, before fees and taxes. Place them from the [order ticket](/docs/trading).
Open pane settings (`PS`) and set **P&L From** to a date. P&L and each holding's contribution then run from the close before it.
Add `DIV%` and `EX-DIV` under **Columns** in `PS`. To compare payers, run `DVD KO,PEP,JNJ`.

pages.title: Trading
pages.lead: Place, change and cancel orders at your broker from one ticket beside the chart.

blocks.alt: Gloom's order ticket beside an AAPL chart, on a simulation account
blocks.caption: A simulation account: draft limit, working stop and average cost on the chart.

blocks.text: Trading needs the desktop app or the terminal.

items: **SnapTrade** (built in): stocks and ETFs at the brokerages it supports. Link them at [dashboard.snaptrade.com](https://dashboard.snaptrade.com), then add **SnapTrade** in Brokers (`BR`) and allow trading.
**[Aries](/plugins/aries)**: stocks, ETFs, options and spreads. Install it from `PL`, add it in `BR` and press **Connect**. Start with **Simulation only**.

**[Interactive Brokers](/plugins/ibkr-gateway)**: trades from the IBKR Gateway plugin's own Trade tab, with Gateway or TWS running ([keeping it logged in](/answers/ib-gateway-daily-restart-sunday-login)).

blocks.text: Then turn on **Enable trading** in the ticket or in `BR`.
A profile with several accounts can leave some out: press `e` on it in `BR` and untick them. Gloom then shows no portfolio for them, does not sync them and does not offer them for orders.

items: In a ticker's research pane, press `t` on the Chart tab.
In the command bar: `BUY AAPL 10`, or `SELL AAPL 10 350` with a limit price.
For options, press `t` on a contract in `OMON`, or on a spread in `OSA`.

blocks.text: `1` to `4` pick market, limit, stop or stop limit. `b` and `s` switch between buy and sell, `r` reviews.
Press `c` beside a price, then click the chart to set it. Drag a dashed line to move a draft price, or a working order's line to change it. Every change goes through review first.

items: Review shows the broker's preview of cost and fees before anything is sent.
Accounts are marked **SIM** or **LIVE**. A live order waits until you type its symbol.
Cancelling asks first, and the order can still fill before the broker confirms.

blocks.text: Open orders sit under the ticket, with edit and cancel, and show on the chart. `ORD` lists orders and fills for every trading account, and fills sync to your portfolio.

pages.title: Alerts
pages.lead: Set price, move and event alerts in ALRT, and know which ones reach you with the app closed.

blocks.code:
SA AAPL above 250
SA QQQ moves 5%
SA EWJ/ACWI above 0.60

blocks.text: The last one follows the ratio of two listings. On a chart, press `Shift+A` on a level to alert there.
Open `ALRT`, go to **Levels** and press `a`. Besides **Price**, you can pick **Move from previous close**, **P/E**, **P/S**, **RSI**, **MA crossover** or **Close vs MA**.

Run **Add Event Alert** to follow earnings dates, CPI and FOMC, SEC filings, news keywords, analyst changes, insider trades, Congress trades, 13F filings and IPOs. They show under **Events**. Options flow and IV spike alerts need Pro.

items: **Price, move, valuation and technical alerts:** the running app checks them. Signed in with Cloud sync on, Gloom Cloud also checks them and reaches your phone and email.
**Earnings, CPI and FOMC dates, and IV levels:** the running app checks them every 15 minutes. Earnings alerts also reach your phone.
**Every other event alert:** Gloom Cloud checks it for a signed-in account and sends it to your phone.

blocks.text: A level alert fires once, then reads **Triggered** until you re-arm it with `m`. A move alert re-arms itself for the next session. **History** lists what went off on this device, and `v` opens what a row follows.

pages.title: AI workflows
pages.lead: Ask Gloom about your panes, turn plain English into commands, screen a theme and run agent threads.

blocks.text: Run `ASKG` with a question, such as `ASKG why is NVDA down today`. It reads your panes and runs research tools. To ask about one pane, press `Alt+A` or choose **Ask Gloom** in its pane menu.
Verified accounts get 20 questions a day, Pro 300. The count resets at midnight UTC.
Plain English in the command bar
Type what you want, such as `compare apple and microsoft margins`, and the command bar suggests the commands under **Ask AI**. This needs a verified account.

Install the [BYOK AI](/plugins/byok-ai) plugin from `PL`, then connect Claude, ChatGPT, the OpenAI API, Gemini, GitHub Copilot, xAI or OpenRouter in pane settings (`PS`). It runs in the desktop app and the terminal, and adds:

items: `AI <theme>`: candidate tickers for an investment theme, one reason each. Check them before acting.
**Ask AI** in Ticker Research: questions about the ticker you are on.
`AGENT`: saved threads that read the app, open panes and change selections. They act at once, with no approval step.

blocks.alt: The AI Agent workspace over an AAPL chart
blocks.caption: Each thread has its own provider and model.

blocks.text: Scripts and outside agents: [Remote control](/docs/agents) and the [MCP server](/docs/mcp).

pages.title: Gloom Cloud
pages.lead: Free, Pro and Team plans, sign-in, chat, the calendar feed, the live toggle, and what stays on your machine.

blocks.text: Gloom Cloud is the optional account behind the app. The app runs without it.

items: **Free:** US stocks and options 15 minutes delayed, news 12 hours delayed, sync, chat and the AI command bar.
**Pro:** real-time US stocks and options, the real-time news wire, options flow, call transcripts, [hiring data](/docs/hiring-data) and the [MCP server](/docs/mcp). 7-day free trial.
**Team:** Pro for every member, billed to the team. See [Teams](/docs/teams).

blocks.text: [Prices](/cloud#pricing) and [data coverage](/data-coverage) are on the site.
The first launch asks you to sign in: by email, `b` for the browser, or `s` to stay local. Later, run **Log In** from the command bar.
**Log In with QR Code** shows a code to scan, then you approve at gloom.sh/link.
A verified email turns on sync, chat and the AI command bar. `ACM` manages your account.

`UPGRADE` opens Pro checkout, or the billing portal during a trial. To cancel a trial or a subscription, use **Cancel Trial** or **Cancel Pro** in `ACM` > Pro, or [gloom.sh/cloud/account](/cloud/account).

items: `CHAT` opens the chat with the most unread messages. `CHAT #macro` opens a public channel.
`DM @alice` starts a direct message, and `DM @alice @bob` a group chat. Each person needs **Incoming DMs** on, under Profile in `ACM`.

blocks.text: A private link with earnings, ex-dividend dates and major US releases for what you hold and watch, free on every plan. Copy it from `ACM` > Calendar (`c`) into Google, Apple or Outlook Calendar. `n` replaces a leaked link.
Charts, quotes, options and portfolios have a lightning toggle. On, they update continuously where your plan allows. Off, once a minute.

items: The app and plugins run on your machine.
Layouts, portfolios, watchlists and settings stay local, and sync across devices once you sign in.
Notes move to Gloom Cloud once you are verified, so [teams](/docs/teams#what-is-shared) can share them.
Sync never uploads broker credentials or other secrets.

blocks.text: The app sends crash reports and counts of how often each function opens, never tickers, portfolios or searches. Signed in, the searches you finish are saved to improve search until you delete your account.
**Crash Reports** and **Usage Counts** in the command bar turn them off.
**Attention Counts** counts the tickers you open toward published totals, never per person. It is on after a one-time notice, and the command of the same name turns it off.

pages.title: Teams
pages.lead: Share layouts, watchlists, notes and a private chat channel with a group, while personal content stays personal.

blocks.text: A team shares layouts, watchlists, paper portfolios, notes and chat channels. Team content sits beside yours in the team's colour.
Creating a team needs Pro. Joining is free, and a team holds up to 25 members. On the Team plan everyone gets Pro while they are a member: [contact us](/contact?topic=team) to set one up.
Create a team and invite people
Run `TEAM`. With no team yet, it opens a short wizard, and the team gets a `#general` channel. Then invite people:

items: `TEAM invite link`: a link that lasts seven days, optionally capped to a number of uses.
`TEAM invite @name`: someone on Gloom. They accept from `TEAM`.
An email address: someone not on Gloom yet.

blocks.text: Owners and admins invite and manage members. Members publish layouts and edit shared notes, watchlists and portfolios.

items: **Layouts:** publishing a tab makes a team layout. Opening it gives you a linked tab with shared content and your own arrangement.
**Watchlists and paper portfolios** update live. Broker-linked portfolios stay personal.
**Notes** have a section per team.
**Views:** a `VIEW` pane published to the team becomes a template for everyone.

blocks.text: Broker positions, credentials and AI threads never travel with a team layout.
Leaving a team removes its channel, notes and lists from your app, and linked tabs become personal copies. `FOCUS` shows only personal content, one team, or all.

pages.title: Company KPIs and guidance
pages.lead: KPIS shows the operating metrics a company discloses, and GUIDE shows what management has guided to and how it turned out

items: `KPIS NVDA`: the operating metrics the company discloses
`GUIDE NVDA`: what management guided to, and how it turned out

blocks.text: Share classes read the same data: `KPIS GOOG` and `KPIS GOOGL`.

items: **Table** (**Tracker** in `GUIDE`): one row per metric with its value, period and trend. `GUIDE` adds the range, issue date, actual and outcome.
**Chart:** the selected series over time.
**Evidence:** the quote from the company's document. `o` opens it.

blocks.text: Both are Pro. Free previews the latest three metrics or guides. Pro adds full history, restatements and filters.

items: Each metric keeps the company's own definition, so similar names are not comparable across companies.
A guide is matched to an actual only when period, units and basis agree. Otherwise it shows unavailable, not a miss.

pages.title: Credit documents and covenants
pages.lead: CRDOC lists a company's loans and bonds with balances, maturities and terms, and COVN shows its covenant tests and the room left

items: `CRDOC FICO`: the company's loans and bonds
`COVN IVZ`: its covenant tests
**Capital:** each facility and bond with balance, coupon and maturity. Enter opens its terms.
**Covenants:** each threshold beside the company's reported figure, with headroom where it can be shown.
**Maturities:** principal by year and currency.
**Screen:** companies with low headroom or a springing maturity coming up.

blocks.text: Both are Pro. Free previews three instruments and three rows per section. Pro shows every term, amendment and the screen.

items: Headroom shows only when the reported figure matches the covenant's definition and is under about six months old. Negative headroom is a disclosed breach, not a default forecast.
A company that is missing is not covered yet. It does not mean it has no debt.

pages.title: Catalysts and litigation
pages.lead: CATL is a calendar of clinical, regulatory, legal and trade-policy events that can move a company, and LITI shows one company's cases

items: `CATL`: the calendar across companies
`CATL PFE`: one company's events
`LITI AAPL`: one company's litigation, enforcement and antitrust cases
**Calendar** (**Dockets** in `LITI`): events by date, type, agency and country. **Upcoming** hides past ones.
**Changes:** recent material changes, such as a trial's status or results.

blocks.text: Enter opens an event with its evidence and every revision. `o` opens the source, `a` sets an alert.
Both are Pro. Free previews three events with their evidence. Pro shows every event, its history and alerts.

items: Announced, effective and deadline dates differ, and an estimated completion date is not a results date.
A complaint or investigation is not a finding of liability.

pages.title: Government awards
pages.lead: AWARDS shows government contracts won by listed companies, with each company's history and awards compared with its revenue

items: `AWARDS`: recent awards across companies
`AWARDS LMT`: one company
**Feed:** new awards and changes to them.
**Company:** one company's awards and the agencies it depends on.
**Agencies** and **Sectors:** who buys from whom, and companies by procurement category.
**Events:** awards that are large against annual revenue.

blocks.text: Enter opens an award with its source and revisions. **Obligated** is what is committed so far; **Ceiling** is the most the contract could be worth.
Both are Pro. Free shows three rows per section. Pro adds filters, history, revisions and relationships.

pages.title: MCP server
pages.lead: Gloom Cloud's [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server at `https://api.gloom.sh/mcp` has the research tools Gloom's own assistant uses.

blocks.text: With access, it also reaches your notes, [teams](/docs/teams) and brokers, and with Terminal control your open app.
Part of [Gloom Pro](/cloud). The same keys work for the [REST API](/docs/rest-api) and [Google Sheets](/docs/google-sheets).
**Sign in from the client.** Claude Code, claude.ai, Cursor and most recent clients need only the endpoint. The first call opens a browser tab where you choose what the client may reach.

blocks.code: claude mcp add --transport http gloom https://api.gloom.sh/mcp

blocks.text: **Or use a key**, for scripts and clients without a browser. Create one in [Cloud settings, Agents](/cloud/account?view=agents) and send it as a bearer token. Keys are shown once, and you can hold up to 10.

blocks.code:
export GLOOM_MCP_KEY=gloom_mcp_...
codex mcp add gloom --url https://api.gloom.sh/mcp --bearer-token-env-var GLOOM_MCP_KEY

blocks.text: **Market data** reaches the research tools. **Read** adds teams, notes, collections and [brokers](#brokers), and **Read and write** saves notes and edits lists. [Terminal control](#terminal-control) is a separate tick. `tools/list` returns only what the caller may call.

items: Creating keys needs Pro. Any valid key can `initialize` and `tools/list`, but tool calls need Pro, except `portfolio.*`.
Keys allow 120 requests a minute and 5,000 a day. Over the limit returns `429` with `Retry-After`.
If Pro lapses, keys stay but tool calls are refused.
Results are capped at 256 KB.

blocks.text: Read-only unless marked write. `tools/list` gives each tool's arguments.
`notes.save` replaces the whole note, so pass the `expectedRevision` you read. A newer edit returns `revision_conflict`.

Terminal control drives your open, signed-in app through the [remote API](/docs/agents). `terminal.snapshot` reads the screen, `terminal.pane.screenshot` returns a pane as a PNG, and one `terminal.*` tool covers each remote operation.
The app asks once before an assistant takes over. Commands, button presses and anything that leaves the app, such as an order, ask on every call. Revoke an assistant in Account Management, Agents.
A broker you connect in Gloom reaches every client with Read access. The `portfolio.*` tools cover all of them in one call and need no Pro.
Interactive Brokers adds `ibkr.*`, and Robinhood adds `robinhood.*`. An IBKR order instruction returns a link where you review and submit it yourself.

IBKR allows one AI connection per user, and Gloom holds it: connecting IBKR here disconnects other AI apps. The IBKR sign-in ends seven days after you consent, and signing in again starts a new seven days.
Each call returns text plus `structuredContent` with `status`, `rowCount`, `truncated`, `asOf` and `data`.

pages.title: Agents and remote control
pages.lead: Use the semantic remote API to inspect and control a running Gloom desktop or TUI session.

blocks.text: `gloom remote` lets a script or local agent drive a Gloom app on this machine: read the screen, open panes, pick tickers and arrange layouts. No account, no network.

blocks.code:
# one terminal: the app
gloom
# another: the agent guide, then what is on screen
gloom remote help
gloom remote get app://snapshot --json

blocks.text: Pass `--app tui` or `--app desktop` when both run. For Claude Code or Codex, the [MCP server](/docs/mcp) with Terminal control gives the same operations.

blocks.code:
# resources, operations and their shapes
gloom remote schema
gloom remote get <resource>
gloom remote call <operation> [json] [--dry-run]
# JSON Patch a mutable resource
gloom remote patch <resource> <json-patch> [--expect-rev rev] [--dry-run]
gloom remote batch <json> [--dry-run]
gloom remote watch <resource> [--interval ms]

blocks.text: With `--json`, a failure exits 1 with an `error.code`, such as `app_not_running` or `app_unreachable` (often a sandbox that blocks localhost).

`app://snapshot` has the layouts, panes, focus, command bar, any open form and the labelled controls. `app://pane-state/{paneId}` has what a pane loaded. In the desktop app, `pane.screenshot` returns a pane as a PNG.

blocks.code:
gloom remote call pane.createFromTemplate '{ "templateId": "market-heatmap-pane" }' --json
gloom remote call ticker.pin '{ "symbol": "NVDA", "forceNewPane": true }' --json

blocks.text: Or run `app.search`, then `commandBar.activateResult`, as the command bar does. `remote batch` sends both in one call.

blocks.code:
gloom remote call layout.setGrid '{ "columns": 2 }' --json
gloom remote call layout.closeFloating '{}' --json

blocks.text: `remote patch` edits config, the current layout, and a pane's state or settings. Pass the `rev` you read as `--expect-rev`, so a stale edit fails instead of overwriting.
With no operation for it, target a UI node by role, label, text or action. Prefer operations: they survive UI changes.

blocks.code: gloom remote call ui.invokeMatching '{ "role": "button", "label": "Open Help", "action": "press" }' --json

blocks.text: On a new profile, `app://form` reads `"kind": "setup"`. Fill it with `ui.invokeMatching` on each `form-field`, or press **Skip**.
Every operation changes only the local app, except `capability.invoke`, which runs a plugin capability and can reach outside services.

pages.title: Google Sheets
pages.lead: =GLOOM and =GLOOMH in Google Sheets: live prices, fundamentals and history with Bloomberg tickers and field names.

items: Create a key with **Market data only** access in [Cloud settings, Agents](/cloud/account?view=agents). It needs [Gloom Pro](/cloud).
In your sheet, open **Extensions > Apps Script**.
Replace everything in `Code.gs` with [gloom.sh/sheets/gloom.js](https://gloom.sh/sheets/gloom.js) and save.
Reload the sheet, choose **Gloom > Set API key** and paste the key. If Google says the script is unverified, choose **Advanced**, then **Go to** your project.
Type `=GLOOM("AAPL US Equity", "PX_LAST")` in a cell.

blocks.text: Only Market data only keys work here, since every editor can read the key.
Or fill the whole table from one cell: `=GLOOM(A2:A3, B1:C1)`.
History, with dates down the first column: `=GLOOMH("CL1 Comdty", "PX_LAST", "2026-01-01", TODAY(), "weekly")`. The period is `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, `quarterly` or `annual`.
A Bloomberg workbook ports with find and replace: `BDP(` to `GLOOM(`, `BDH(` to `GLOOMH(`. Tickers and fields are the [REST API's](/docs/rest-api).
Coming from Bloomberg? [BDP and BDH next to their Sheets formulas](/answers/bloomberg-bdp-bdh-google-sheets).

items: A missing value reads `#N/A` with the reason, so `IFERROR` does not hide it. Use `ISNUMBER`.
All `GLOOM` cells fetch together, so hundreds of cells cost a few requests.
Prices refresh after a minute, other values after an hour. **Gloom > Refresh data** fetches again.
A revoked key, a free plan or the rate limit shows in the cells and pauses fetching for a few minutes.

pages.title: News API
pages.lead: Use Gloom's standalone market-news API in your own financial product.

blocks.code:
curl -s 'https://api.gloom.sh/v1/news?feed=top&limit=25' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer gloom_news_...'

blocks.text: The News API is Gloom's market news for your own product, billed apart from [Gloom Cloud](/docs/cloud-and-data). The [financial news API](/news) page shows the live wire and has the **Get API key** button.

items: **Free key:** news 12 hours delayed, with the full response. Create or rotate it in your [News API account](/news/account).
**Real-time:** from $199 a month with the [News and our own data plan](/datasets/pricing#news). Existing Unlimited subscriptions keep real-time access.

blocks.text: Send the key as `Authorization: Bearer` or `x-api-key`. A [Gloom Datasets](/docs/datasets) key (`gds_`) works too. `GET /v1/me` returns your plan and delay.

rows: How closely a story is tied to the ticker

blocks.code:
curl -s 'https://api.gloom.sh/v1/news?feed=ticker&tickers=NVDA:XNAS&tickerTier=primary' \
  -H 'x-api-key: gloom_news_...'

blocks.text: `GET /v1/news/{storyId}` returns one story with its source items.
Abridged: each story also carries topics, sectors and flags.

Ticker problems return `400` with a `reasonCode`: `TICKERS_REQUIRED` when `feed=ticker` has no `tickers`, or `AMBIGUOUS_TICKER`, where `candidates` lists the exchange-qualified symbols to send instead.

pages.title: Gloom Datasets
pages.lead: GPU prices, supply chains, hiring and attention signals alongside filings, macro, news and market data. One paid REST API. Every value cited.

blocks.text: Gloom Datasets serves the data Gloom stores to your own systems over REST. It is a separate product, with its own [site](/datasets), keys and plans.

items: **Alternative data:** GPU rental prices, supply chain, hiring postings and momentum, social mentions, app attention, power and grid, perpetuals, catalysts and litigation, congressional trades, operating exposure.
**Filings and company text:** KPIs and guidance, executive pay, risk factors, 8-K events, transcripts, credit documents, SEC filings, insiders and 13F.
**News:** real-time stories, sources and topics.
**Macro and positioning:** CPI, energy inventories, COT, yield curves, central bank rates, short interest, CDS, government awards.
**Market data:** quotes, history, financial statements, estimates, options and gamma positioning, futures and crypto.

blocks.text: Every call returns `data` and `meta`, which carries attribution, usage terms and `asOf`. A value the data cannot establish is `null`.

items: Create a key in the [console](/datasets/console). Keys start with `gds_`, and Free needs no card.
Send it as `Authorization: Bearer gds_...` to `https://api.gloom.sh/v1`.
Follow the [quickstart](/datasets/docs/quickstart) for the first call from curl, Python or TypeScript.

blocks.text: Free reads company data on 10 popular tickers, and market-wide data such as macro and rates on every name, for the last 30 days: 100 calls a day.
Paid plans start at $49 a month, for one band of datasets or all of them. Each call spends credits, and `X-Credits-Remaining` says what is left. See [Pricing](/datasets/pricing).
A Gloom Pro key (`gloom_mcp_`) or a News API key gets `401 wrong_key` on a dataset route. A `gds_` key does not work on the [REST API](/docs/rest-api).
A paid plan's `gds_` key does read the [News API](/docs/news-api), at no credit cost. The [API reference](/datasets/docs) has every route.
