pages.lead: Install, build and publish Gloom plugins: panes, commands, CLI commands, data capabilities and UI.

blocks.text: A plugin can add panes, commands, CLI commands, data capabilities and brokers. The full API is in [PLUGINS.md](https://github.com/gloom-sh/gloomberb/blob/main/PLUGINS.md).
In the app, `PL` lists plugins and toggles them. Typing the code of an official plugin you lack, such as `TV`, offers to install it.

blocks.caption: PL toggles first-party and installed plugins.

blocks.code:
gloom install user/repo
gloom update
gloom remove my-plugin
# why a plugin does not load
gloom plugin doctor my-plugin

blocks.text: Restart Gloom after a CLI install or an edit.
Create `hello-gloom/index.ts`. It adds one command-bar command and one shell command:
Link it and run the shell command:

blocks.code:
gloom plugin link ./hello-gloom
gloom hello Vince --json

blocks.text: Restart Gloom, then type `HELLO` in the command bar. For an interactive pane, copy [gloom-hackernews](https://github.com/gloom-sh/gloom-hackernews).
[gloom.sh/plugins](/plugins) lists every public repo with the `gloom-plugin` topic. Describe the plugin in `gloom.json` at the repo's root:
`id` is required. `targets` says where it runs, `hosts` which domains it talks to, and `icon` is a square image in the repo.
The directory is a listing, not a review. Tag each release, since `install` and `update` use the latest tag.

lessons.title: What a stock is
lessons.summary: A share is a small slice of a company, so owning one means owning a tiny piece of everything the company has and earns.

lessons.title: Funds, ETFs and indices
lessons.summary: A fund is a basket you can own, an index is a ruler that measures a basket, and an ETF is a fund that trades like a stock.

lessons.title: Exchanges, hours and tickers
lessons.summary: An exchange is the marketplace where shares change hands during set hours, and every listed security has a short code called a ticker.

lessons.title: Reading a quote
lessons.summary: A quote is not one price but five numbers (last trade, best bid, best ask, the spread between them, and volume) that together tell you what you would really pay to trade now.

lessons.title: Orders, long, short and margin
lessons.summary: An order is your instruction to a broker, and long, short and margin say which way you bet and whether you borrowed to do it.

lessons.title: Returns and percentages
lessons.summary: A return is the gain or loss compared with what you paid, written as a percentage so that a 20 dollar stock and a 2,000 dollar stock can be compared.

lessons.title: Understanding risk
lessons.summary: Four numbers describe how much an investment can hurt: volatility (how bumpy), drawdown (how deep the worst fall), correlation (do two things move together) and beta (how much it moves with the market).

lessons.title: Who is who on Wall Street
lessons.summary: Wall Street is a few kinds of players: the buy side invests money, the sell side sells it services and trades, the plumbing (market makers, prime brokers, clearing) makes trades happen and settle, and regulators watch them all.

lessons.title: How information reaches prices
lessons.summary: Prices move when new information (results, filings, economic numbers, central bank decisions, news) differs from what people already expected: only the surprise moves the price.

lessons.title: The macro machine
lessons.summary: "Macro" is the economy as a whole (output, inflation and jobs) plus the interest rate the central bank sets to steer them, and it is why one number can move every market at once.

lessons.title: Derivatives in one page
lessons.summary: A derivative is a contract whose value comes from something else (a stock, an index, oil, an interest rate), and the three big families are futures, options and swaps.

lessons.title: Bonds in one page
lessons.summary: A bond is a loan you can buy and sell, paying fixed interest until a set repayment date, and its price and its yield always move in opposite directions.

lessons.title: The cheat sheet
lessons.summary: The whole chapter on one page, to re-read before a meeting: a 100-word summary, the numbers to remember and who is who.

lessons.title: Your first 10 minutes
lessons.summary: Gloom is a grid of screens you open by typing a short code and a ticker; in ten minutes you can set up your holdings, open a company, see what moves today, set an alert and find help.

lessons.title: The command bar and function codes
lessons.summary: The command bar is the one place you type everything: a function code, then what it applies to (DES AAPL), or plain words to search; it answers "how do I open X?".

lessons.title: Tickers, listings and asset classes
lessons.summary: The same company can trade under several tickers on several exchanges, so Gloom lets you pick the exact listing with a suffix or a search and filter by asset class.

lessons.title: Panes, focus and linking (WIN, GL, PS, LMA)
lessons.summary: Every function opens in a pane, one pane at a time has the focus and receives your keys, and panes can be moved, stacked as tabs, tidied, given a new ticker and linked so they follow a list.

lessons.title: Layouts and desks (LAY, DESK)
lessons.summary: A layout is a saved screen of panes, DESK adds a ready-made one for a kind of market, and LAY switches, adds and shares layouts.

lessons.title: Getting help (HELP, F1, CHG, FB)
lessons.summary: HELP opens the guide and every function, and F1 opens the help card of the pane in front of you, including how fresh its data is on your plan.

lessons.title: Free, Pro and how fresh your data is (UPGRADE, CONN)
lessons.summary: Every number has an age (real-time, 15 minutes behind, daily or on release), and the help card's Data line and the clock mark on a quote tell you which.

lessons.title: Gloom from your shell (the CLI)
lessons.summary: The functions you open in panes also run from your computer's command line, printing a table or JSON and CSV for scripts and spreadsheets.

lessons.title: Make it yours (VIEW, PL, TH, LANG, FONT, SB, VF, CR)
lessons.summary: VIEW builds your own table from any data function, PL manages plugins, and a few short commands change the theme, language, font size and visual effects.

lessons.title: Portfolios and watchlists (PF, AP, AW, RP, RW)
lessons.summary: PF shows what you own (positions, cost, profit and loss) and what you follow (watchlists) with live prices, and AP, AW, RP and RW add or remove tickers from anywhere.

lessons.title: Portfolio risk (PORT, MARS)
lessons.summary: PORT (also MARS) measures your portfolio's risk against a benchmark: how much it swings, its worst fall, a bad-day loss estimate, which holdings move together, and what a crash or a rate jump would do to it.

lessons.title: How big a position? (KELLY)
lessons.summary: KELLY turns your own guesses (chance of being right, upside, downside) into a position size, caps it with your risk limits, and says how much to add or trim.

lessons.title: Alerts (ALRT, SA)
lessons.summary: An alert watches the market for you, firing on a price level, a day's move, a valuation or technical level, or an event such as an earnings date, a filing or an insider trade, and ALRT lists them all.

lessons.title: Notes and theses (NOTE, THESIS)
lessons.summary: Notes are your free-form memory (NOTE), and a thesis (THESIS) is a checkable reason for holding something, with pillars that must stay true and kill conditions that would make you sell.

lessons.title: Chat and teams (CHAT, DM, TEAM)
lessons.summary: CHAT opens public channels by topic, DM @user starts a private conversation, and TEAM creates a private group that shares layouts, lists, notes and its own chat.

lessons.title: Your account and your broker (ACM, BR, IBKR)
lessons.summary: ACM manages your Gloom account, and BR connects a brokerage account so your real positions appear in a portfolio and stay in sync.

lessons.title: The AI helpers (ASKG, AI, AGENT)
lessons.summary: Gloom has three AI helpers: Ask Gloom (ASKG) answers with Gloom's own tools and cites its sources, the AI screener (AI) turns a sentence into a list of tickers, and the agent (AGENT) can operate the app for you.

lessons.title: The overview page (DES)
lessons.summary: DES is the front page of a ticker: quote, day and 52-week ranges, the long chart, returns, key numbers, and tabs into everything else, on one screen.

lessons.title: A board of quotes (QQ)
lessons.summary: QQ is a wall of tiles, one per ticker, each with the last price, today's change, a one-month sparkline and the month's low and high.

lessons.title: A fund's facts and official documents (ETF)
lessons.summary: ETF shows a US fund's facts (fee, NAV, premium or discount, net assets), then lists its filings with the SEC (prospectus, holdings reports, shareholder reports) and opens any of them.

lessons.title: Earnings ripple (RIPL)
lessons.summary: RIPL lists the big customers and suppliers of your holdings that report earnings in the next 30 days, with how much revenue links them.

lessons.title: Reading a price chart (GP)
lessons.summary: GP is the price chart: candles on top, volume below, a multi-year range by default.

lessons.title: The intraday chart (GIP)
lessons.summary: GIP charts one trading session (or the last five) minute by minute, with volume below and the session's start and end marked.

lessons.title: Moving averages, RSI and MACD (chart indicators)
lessons.summary: Indicators are formulas on past prices drawn on the chart: moving averages smooth the noise, RSI measures how one-sided recent moves were, and MACD compares a fast average with a slow one.

lessons.title: VWAP, bands, ATR and price levels (chart tools)
lessons.summary: VWAP, Bollinger Bands, ATR, volume profile and your own price levels are different ways of asking whether today's price is normal, and a level can become an alert.

lessons.title: Chart anything together (G)
lessons.summary: G puts any series (a price, a statement line, a multiple, an economic series or a formula) on one timeline so you can see whether they move together.

lessons.title: The price history table (HP)
lessons.summary: HP is the chart turned into rows: one line per bar with open, high, low, close, the change from the bar before, and volume.

lessons.title: The returns table (RETURN)
lessons.summary: RETURN lists the return of each period and the return since the start of the window, so you can see how small moves compound.

lessons.title: Seasonality (SEAS)
lessons.summary: SEAS lays out a ticker's monthly returns year by year with each month's average, median and share of up years, and shows why calendar patterns are weak evidence.

lessons.title: Backtesting a rule (BT, BTST)
lessons.summary: BT (also BTST) replays a simple buy-and-sell rule on a stock's daily history and compares it with buying and holding, trade by trade.

lessons.title: The trade tape (TAS)
lessons.summary: TAS (time and sales) lists every reported trade in a US stock as it prints, with time, price, shares, venue and conditions, and the VWAP of the trades seen.

lessons.title: The best bid and ask over time (QR)
lessons.summary: QR (quote recap) shows every change in the best bid and ask across US exchanges, with sizes, venues and the spread in basis points.

lessons.title: The three financial statements (FA)
lessons.summary: Every company reports three tables (the income statement, the balance sheet and the cash flow statement), and FA shows all three by year or quarter.

lessons.title: Ratios that matter (FA ratio tabs)
lessons.summary: A ratio divides one number by another so companies of any size can be compared: margins and returns for quality, debt ratios for risk, and valuation multiples for price.

lessons.title: Red and green flags (DIAG)
lessons.summary: DIAG turns a company's filings and numbers into a short verdict and lists of red flags, green flags and items to watch, each with the fact, a reading and its source filing.

lessons.title: Revenue by segment and company KPIs (SEG, KPIS)
lessons.summary: SEG splits a company's revenue by product, segment and region from its filings, and KPIS tracks the operating numbers it reports beyond the statements, each with its source quote.

lessons.title: What growth is priced in? (RDCF)
lessons.summary: RDCF runs a discounted cash flow model backwards, finding the yearly growth today's value assumes and setting it next to the growth the company actually delivered.

lessons.title: The earnings calendar and implied moves (ERN, EVTS)
lessons.summary: EVTS lists who reports this week with the move options are pricing and the move the stock usually makes, and ERN <ticker> shows one company's next report and its history.

lessons.title: Estimates, surprises and revisions (EE, EM)
lessons.summary: EE sets analysts' consensus estimates next to the results actually reported, and EM tracks how that consensus is being revised.

lessons.title: Guidance (GUID, GUIDE)
lessons.summary: Guidance is the company's own forecast, and GUID and GUIDE set it next to the consensus and track each guided number, its raises and cuts, and the actual result.

lessons.title: Earnings calls (CALLS)
lessons.summary: CALLS lists a company's earnings calls and opens each transcript with speakers, the analyst Q&A, a tone score, and the guidance and quotes pulled out of it.

lessons.title: Analyst ratings and price targets (ANR)
lessons.summary: ANR shows sell-side ratings and 12-month price targets: the average target and its history, the upside to it, and every recent action by firm.

lessons.title: Dividends and corporate actions (DVD, EVT)
lessons.summary: DVD shows a stock's dividend history, yield, payout ratio and growth, and EVT puts dividends, splits, earnings dates and estimates on one timeline.

lessons.title: Catalysts (CATL)
lessons.summary: CATL is a calendar of dated events that can move a stock (trial results, regulators' decisions, court deadlines, tariffs), each with its date basis, status and source.

lessons.title: Mergers and acquisitions (MA)
lessons.summary: MA lists pending, rumored and closed takeover deals with their terms, their stage and, for listed targets, the arbitrage spread between the offer and the market price.

lessons.title: Comparing returns (CMP)
lessons.summary: CMP draws two or more tickers as percentage returns from the same start date, so you can see which did better over the same window.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Relative valuation (RV)
lessons.summary: RV puts a peer group in one table at today's prices (size, P/E, forward P/E, EV/sales, free cash flow yield and growth) so you can judge a company's price against its peers.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Valuation over time (GE, GF, PEB)
lessons.summary: PEB, GE and GF turn valuation snapshots into history: a stock's price against fixed P/E lines, multiples over time for several tickers, and statement lines across companies.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: How stocks move together (GR, CORR)
lessons.summary: GR studies how two tickers move together (ratio, rolling correlation, regression) and CORR builds a correlation matrix for a whole basket.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Screening the market (EQS)
lessons.summary: EQS keeps only the stocks in its stored universe that meet all your rules (valuation, growth, margins, liquidity, ownership and more) and ranks the matches.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Value, quality and GARP screens (EQS)
lessons.summary: Three of the ready screens in EQS write three styles of stock picking as rules: Value looks for cash bought cheaply, Quality for businesses that earn a high return on their capital, and GARP for steady growth at a price the growth can carry.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Classic value and quality scores (EQS)
lessons.summary: Four classic scores each turn the statements into one number: Piotroski's F-score (getting stronger?), Altman's Z (how far from distress?), the Graham number (the most a careful buyer pays) and the Magic Formula (good businesses at cheap prices).
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Grades within a sector (EQS)
lessons.summary: EQS grades every covered company from F to A+ on Value, Growth, Profitability, Momentum and Revisions against the other companies in its sector, and blends the five into a composite from Bottom to Top.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Your own intraday scan (SCAN)
lessons.summary: SCAN watches US stocks through the trading day and lists the ones that match your intraday conditions right now (a fast move, a burst of volume, a new high or low, a VWAP cross, a gap), and can alert you when a new one appears.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Big holders and 13F filings (HDS, 13F)
lessons.summary: HDS shows a stock's biggest institutional holders from quarterly 13F filings, and 13F browses the funds themselves: holdings, changes, crowded positions and estimated performance.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Insider trades (INS)
lessons.summary: INS lists the trades company insiders must report on Form 4 within two business days (buys, sells, awards, gifts and tax payments) with name, size and price.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Congress trades (CG)
lessons.summary: CG lists the trades members of Congress must disclose within 45 days, with the member, the asset, buy or sell, the amount band, the owner and how late it was reported.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Short interest and squeezes (SI, SIV, SIW)
lessons.summary: SI shows short interest over time with days to cover, SIV the daily short share of off-exchange volume (a noisier number), and SIW ranks your names by how crowded the short is.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: SEC filings and 8-K events (SEC, EK)
lessons.summary: SEC lists a company's filings on the SEC's public EDGAR database and opens them, and EK reads its 8-K event notices item by item with a short summary of each.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Risk factors (RISK)
lessons.summary: RISK groups the risk factors in a company's 10-K by theme and shows what was added, dropped or reworded since the previous year.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Executive pay (EXEC)
lessons.summary: EXEC reads the yearly proxy statement into key pay figures (CEO total pay, the pay ratio, the share in stock, shareholder support) and a table of the top executives.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Social buzz (BUZZ)
lessons.summary: BUZZ counts the day's posts on X naming a ticker against its usual level, with the top posts and their stance, and alone ranks the tickers whose posts jump most above their own usual level.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: What an option is (calls and puts)
lessons.summary: An option is the right, but not the duty, to buy or sell something at a fixed price before a deadline, and you pay a fee for that right.

lessons.title: Value and payoff at expiry
lessons.summary: An option's price is what it is worth if used right now (intrinsic value) plus a bet on the future (time value), and at expiry only the first part is left.

lessons.title: The Greeks in plain words (OVME)
lessons.summary: The Greeks say how an option's price reacts when the stock moves (delta, gamma), when time passes (theta) or when expected swings change (vega), and OVME computes them for any option you describe.

lessons.title: Implied vs realized volatility
lessons.summary: Realized volatility is how much a stock actually moved and implied volatility is how much option prices assume it will move, and comparing the two is the core question of a volatility desk.

lessons.title: What a volatility desk does
lessons.summary: A bank's volatility desk makes markets in options, hedges away direction every day, and keeps a book of exposures to movement (gamma) and to volatility (vega), earning the spread and, on average, implied above realized volatility.

lessons.title: The options chain (OMON)
lessons.summary: OMON is the menu of every option on one stock: one tab per expiry, one row per strike, calls left and puts right with quotes and Greeks, and a strip of volatility numbers on top.

lessons.title: Building a position (OSA)
lessons.summary: OSA turns several option legs into one position and shows its value at any stock price, date and volatility, with breakevens, maximum profit and loss, and the combined Greeks.

lessons.title: Screening option trades (CSP)
lessons.summary: CSP builds the same option trade on a list of stocks at once (a cash-secured put, a covered call, a spread, a condor, a straddle, a strangle or a calendar) and ranks them, so you can see which name pays most for the risk.

lessons.title: The volatility surface and skew (OVDV)
lessons.summary: Implied volatility changes with the strike (the skew) and with the expiry (the term structure), and OVDV fits the whole surface from option quotes.

lessons.title: Realized volatility and the cone (HVG, HVT)
lessons.summary: HVG charts realized volatility over windows from 10 to 260 sessions, and HVT (the cone) places each window's current value in its own range over the past year or two.

lessons.title: Is implied vol high or low? (HIVG, VCA)
lessons.summary: HIVG charts a stock's implied volatility history with IV rank and percentile, and VCA ranks a list of tickers as rich, fair or cheap on those and a few other clues.

lessons.title: The VIX and volatility indices (VIX, VOLS)
lessons.summary: The VIX is the 30-day implied volatility of the S&P 500, and VIX and VOLS show its curve across horizons and its cousins in bonds, oil, gold and single stocks.

lessons.title: Open interest and max pain (OPX)
lessons.summary: OPX shows open interest (contracts still open) by strike and expiry, with the put/call ratio and max pain, the expiry price at which option holders would collect least.

lessons.title: Dealer gamma (GEX)
lessons.summary: Dealer gamma (GEX) estimates how much option dealers would trade per 1% move to stay hedged, under an assumption about who holds which option, and where that estimate flips sign.

lessons.title: Options flow (FLOW)
lessons.summary: FLOW is a live tape of large option trades on the busiest US contracts (sweeps, blocks and big-premium prints) with ticker, contract, size, premium and implied volatility, plus the session's net premium tide.

lessons.title: Futures from zero (FUT)
lessons.summary: A futures contract is a standard, exchange-traded promise to buy or sell a set quantity on a set month at a price agreed today, settled with daily margin, and FUT shows each market's front month.

lessons.title: Futures curves and rolling (CTM)
lessons.summary: A futures curve lines up every contract month of one commodity, rising (contango) when storing costs money and falling (backwardation) when it is scarce now, and CTM shows it with the cost of rolling.

lessons.title: Who holds the futures (COT)
lessons.summary: The CFTC's weekly Commitments of Traders shows how many futures contracts speculators, hedgers and small traders hold long and short, and COT shows it per market with history and percentiles.

lessons.title: Oil and gas inventories (DOE, NGS)
lessons.summary: DOE and NGS show the weekly US government counts of crude, products and natural gas in storage against last year and the five-year range.

lessons.title: Power and the grid (POWER)
lessons.summary: POWER collects the public queues of power projects and large electricity users waiting to connect to the grid, with their history and outcomes.

lessons.title: GPU rental prices (GPU)
lessons.summary: GPU collects published hourly rental prices for AI chips by model and price basis, with list indexes, medians, history and a daily settle, so compute can be tracked like a commodity.

lessons.title: How a stock reacts on macro days (MDAY)
lessons.summary: MDAY compares how a US listing moves on CPI, jobs and central bank decision days with a normal day, over up to five years, and lists every release day with its figures and move.

lessons.title: The yield curve and its spreads (GC)
lessons.summary: GC draws government yield curves for the US (nominal and real), Germany, the UK, Japan, Canada and the euro AAA curve, with the main slope spreads and their changes.

lessons.title: The Fed path (WIRP)
lessons.summary: WIRP turns the prices of overnight-rate futures into the rate the market expects after each scheduled Fed meeting, with hike or cut probabilities and the Fed's own projections.

lessons.title: Central bank rates around the world (CBR)
lessons.summary: CBR lists the policy rates of the G20 central banks, the SNB, Norges Bank, the Riksbank and the RBNZ with the current level, the last move and its date, and where each rate sits in its past year.

lessons.title: Money markets and liquidity (BTMM)
lessons.summary: BTMM shows where banks, funds and the government borrow for a night to a year: overnight rates, the Treasury bill curve, and the Fed's balance-sheet liquidity.

lessons.title: Treasury auctions (AUCT)
lessons.summary: AUCT lists upcoming and recent US Treasury auctions with the rate each cleared at, how well it was covered and who bought, and Hong Kong's government paper tenders.

lessons.title: Pricing one bond (YAS)
lessons.summary: YAS is a bond calculator that turns a yield into a price (or back) and adds accrued interest, duration, convexity, DV01 and the spread to the Treasury curve.

lessons.title: Credit spreads (CRD)
lessons.summary: A credit spread is the extra yield a company pays over a government bond for the risk of not paying back, and CRD shows the spreads of US corporate bond indices by rating.

lessons.title: Credit default swaps (CDS, CDX, SOVR)
lessons.summary: A credit default swap is insurance on a borrower's default, and CDS, CDX and SOVR show reported trades on companies, the main indices and 5-year country spreads.

lessons.title: Debt maturities and covenants (DDIS, CRDOC, COVN)
lessons.summary: DDIS shows how much of a company's debt comes due each year, and CRDOC and COVN read its loan and bond documents into a capital structure and covenant headroom.

lessons.title: The economic calendar (ECO)
lessons.summary: ECO lists upcoming and recent economic releases and central bank events by time, with their impact and the actual, forecast and prior numbers.
lessons.chapter: The big picture: macro, markets and news

lessons.title: Economic statistics (ECST)
lessons.summary: ECST is a dashboard of the main US economic statistics (inflation, labor, growth, housing, rates), each with its latest value and a chart against its own history.
lessons.chapter: The big picture: macro, markets and news

lessons.title: Inflation by component (CPI)
lessons.summary: CPI breaks US consumer prices into their components with each one's weight, its monthly, annualized and yearly change, and its contribution to the headline.
lessons.chapter: The big picture: macro, markets and news

lessons.title: Currencies and cross rates (FXC)
lessons.summary: FXC is a matrix of exchange rates between the major currencies, each cell saying how many units of the column currency one unit of the row currency buys.
lessons.chapter: The big picture: macro, markets and news

lessons.title: World indices and trading hours (WEI, MAP)
lessons.summary: WEI lists the main stock indices of the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific with their level, change and session status, and MAP shows every trading venue on a world map.
lessons.chapter: The big picture: macro, markets and news

lessons.title: Sectors, themes and rotation (BI, THEM, RRG)
lessons.summary: BI shows sector and industry performance, THEM curated themes as equal-weight baskets with breadth, and RRG plots each sector's strength and momentum against the market.
lessons.chapter: The big picture: macro, markets and news

lessons.title: The market heatmap (HM)
lessons.summary: HM draws the largest US stocks as rectangles sized by market value and colored by today's change.
lessons.chapter: The big picture: macro, markets and news

lessons.title: Movers, new highs and lows, halts (MOST, HILO, HALT)
lessons.summary: MOST lists today's biggest gainers, losers and most active stocks, HILO counts new session highs and lows live, and HALT lists trading halts.
lessons.chapter: The big picture: macro, markets and news

lessons.title: IPOs (IPO)
lessons.summary: IPO lists upcoming, priced and recent initial public offerings on the main US, Asia-Pacific and European venues, with size, price range and first-day performance.
lessons.chapter: The big picture: macro, markets and news

lessons.title: Sentiment and market valuation (FNG, VAL)
lessons.summary: FNG shows a fear-and-greed gauge built from seven market signals, and VAL shows whole-market valuation ratios against their own history.
lessons.chapter: The big picture: macro, markets and news

lessons.title: The news feeds (TOP, N, CN, NI, FIRST)
lessons.summary: Gloom shows one stream of stories five ways: TOP ranks what matters, N shows everything as it arrives, CN filters a company, NI a topic, and FIRST only breaking news.
lessons.chapter: The big picture: macro, markets and news

lessons.title: Social posts, newsletters, TV and tech news (TWIT, SUB, TV, HN)
lessons.summary: Four optional panes bring outside media next to your data: TWIT (a live X search), SUB (your newsletters), TV (live business TV) and HN (Hacker News).
lessons.chapter: The big picture: macro, markets and news

lessons.title: Crypto from zero (CRYP)
lessons.summary: Crypto coins are digital assets recorded on public ledgers and traded around the clock on many venues, and CRYP lists the largest by market cap with price and changes.

lessons.title: Perpetual futures, funding and open interest (PERP)
lessons.summary: A perpetual future never expires and is kept close to its underlying by a periodic funding payment, and PERP shows a market's funding, open interest and premium over time.

lessons.title: Bitcoin and ether options (OPX, OVDV)
lessons.summary: Bitcoin and ether have listed options of their own, and OPX BTC-USD and OVDV BTC-USD read them like a stock's: open interest, max pain, the volatility surface, and DVOL, the 30-day implied volatility index of the coin.

lessons.title: Prediction markets (PM)
lessons.summary: In a prediction market a contract pays 1 dollar if an event happens and 0 if not, so its price in cents reads as the crowd's probability, and PM lists these markets by topic.

lessons.title: Political polls (POLL)
lessons.summary: POLL lists US political polls by type with date, subject, pollster, sample and result, and opens each one with its margin of error and the running average.

lessons.title: Drug safety reports and clinical trials (FDA, TRIAL)
lessons.summary: FDA searches public US reports of drug and device side effects and drug recalls, and TRIAL searches the public registry of clinical studies.

lessons.title: Litigation and SEC comment letters (LITI, CLTR)
lessons.summary: LITI lists a company's lawsuits, enforcement and antitrust cases with their documents and dated status, and CLTR lists the letters SEC staff sent the company about its filings and the replies.

lessons.title: Government contracts and awards (AWARDS)
lessons.summary: AWARDS collects published government contracts from the US, Europe, the UK and elsewhere, matches recipients to listed companies, and shows each award with its value and evidence.

lessons.title: Hiring signals (JOBS, HIRE)
lessons.summary: JOBS reads one company's open roles over time from its own careers site, and HIRE compares hiring momentum across companies.

lessons.title: App store rankings (APPS)
lessons.summary: APPS tracks where a listed company's apps rank on public app-store charts by country and chart, with ratings and an overall attention score.

lessons.title: Supply chains and scenario exposure (SPLC, EXPO)
lessons.summary: SPLC maps a company's customers, suppliers, competitors and investees from filings, announcements and calls with evidence, and EXPO estimates a portfolio's exposure to a shock along those links.

lessons.title: The AI infrastructure map (TBO)
lessons.summary: TBO opens a partner's research database on the physical build-out of AI and semiconductors: a board of themes, the companies in each, physical sites and dated research notes. TBOC follows one company's power deals, suppliers, customers and sites.

lessons.title: Searching calls, news and filings (SRCH)
lessons.summary: SRCH searches earnings-call transcripts, news and SEC filings at once and shows every passage that matches your phrase, with saved searches that can alert you to new matches.
